metaDescription: Six wall mounted and recessed electric fireplaces compared on width, heater output, thermostat range, depth and install needs for living room walls.
expertTake: The Silonn 50 inch smart fireplace is the best overall pick for its app control, 5100 BTU heater and standard width. The Garvee 30 inch is the value pick for a small wall or a stud bay. Anyone who needs real whole room heating should skip electric fireplaces and use a proper heating system.
introParagraphs: A wall mounted electric fireplace gives a living room a glowing focal point without a chimney, a gas line or a hearth. Most plug into a standard outlet, hang like a large picture or sit inside a framed recess, and run the flame display with or without heat.

They are decor first and supplemental heaters second. This guide compares six units on width, heater output, thermostat control and the install work they really need, and is honest about what a plug in fireplace can heat and where it needs space around it.

products.name: Silonn 50 Inch Smart Electric Fireplace, 5100 BTU, Wall Mounted or Recessed
products.description:
Silonn builds a 50 inch ultra slim fireplace that can be mounted on the wall or recessed, with a 1500 watt heater that produces up to 5100 BTU. It connects to a Wi-Fi app, a remote and a touch panel, so you can pre-heat the room before you sit down. The flame has 20 colour modes and a crystal stone ember effect that works with or without heat.

The tradeoff is the usual one for plug in units: 5100 BTU is zone heat for one room, and the fan front heater adds some noise. It also depends on an app for the smart features, which are optional but useful. Against the Tehanld 60 inch, the 50 inch is easier to fit; against the Touchstone Sideline 50, it has more smart control and a larger flame palette.

It suits a sofa wall in a room of roughly 300 to 400 square feet where the fireplace is a heater and a feature. Plan the stud positions, a nearby outlet and the clearance above it before mounting. In year three, expect to vacuum the heater vents, to check the remote battery and to run the flame without heat on warm days to preserve the element.
products.bestFor: A standard sofa wall that wants a smart controlled flame and real supplemental heat.
pros: A 50 inch width suits a three seat sofa or a TV wall
Wi-Fi app and remote let you pre-heat the room
Twenty flame colours and crystal media look rich with or without heat
Can be wall mounted or recessed into framing
cons: Zone heat only, not a whole room or whole house heater
The smart features depend on an app and your Wi-Fi

products.name: LegendFlame Austin 72 Inch Built In Electric Fireplace, In Wall Recessed

specList.label: Overall size
specList.value: 72 W x 18.9 H x 5.8 D in

specList.label: Heater
specList.value: Upper front blower, two heat settings

products.description:
LegendFlame's Austin is a 72 inch wide linear fireplace for building into a wall, with overall dimensions of about 72 by 18.9 by 5.8 inches and an insert width near 70.9 inches. The listing gives full dimensions, which is rare and matters because a recess has to match them. It has multiple flame combinations and a heater at the upper front.

The tradeoff is the install. It is a recessed unit, so you are framing a wall cavity, running power and finishing around the trim, and the size puts it at the top cost tier. It is a rough in project rather than a hang and plug product. Against the Silonn 50, it is wider and more architectural but needs more construction.

It suits a long accent wall or a media wall in a house where you can frame in the unit during a renovation. Check the cavity depth against the 5.8 inch figure and the manual for framing and clearance. In year three, expect to clean the vents, replace remote batteries and check the glass for dust.
products.bestFor: A renovation where a wide, built in linear fireplace anchors the main wall.
pros: A 72 inch width creates a true architectural focal line
Full dimensions in the listing make framing easy to plan
Multiple flame combinations suit different moods
Slim 5.8 inch depth fits a standard wall cavity
cons: A recessed install needs framing and often a contractor
Top cost tier of the group

products.name: Touchstone Sideline 50 Inch Electric Fireplace, In Wall Recessed

specList.label: Install
specList.value: In wall recessed, attaches to framing studs

specList.label: Heat
specList.value: Takes the edge off a cool room

products.description:
Touchstone's Sideline is a 50 inch recessed fireplace that attaches directly to framing studs, with 30 flame and ember colour combinations and the option to run with no heat. The maker describes the heater as taking the edge off a cool room or basement, which is a modest and honest description of supplemental heat. It is a plain, well known model in this category.

The tradeoff is smarts: there is no Wi-Fi app in the listing, so it is a remote operated unit. It is a recessed product, so the wall must be framed for it. Compared with the Silonn 50, it has fewer smart features and a simpler flame set. Against the LegendFlame Austin, it is smaller and easier to fit.

It suits a new wall build or a framed bay where you can screw to studs. Check the stud spacing and depth first. In year three, expect to clean the glass front, vacuum the vents and keep the remote handy.
products.bestFor: Framed walls where a simple, stud mounted 50 inch unit is enough.
pros: Mounts straight to framing studs for a solid fit
Thirty flame and ember combinations give plenty of looks
Runs with no heat for year round ambience
A simple unit with fewer electronics to fail
cons: No app control stated in the listing
Recessed only, so it needs a framed wall cavity

products.name: Tehanld 60 Inch Ultra Thin Electric Fireplace, Recessed or Wall Mounted
products.description:
Tehanld offers a 60 inch ultra thin fireplace with a thermostat from 60 to 99 degrees Fahrenheit, three heat settings of off, 750 and 1500 watts, and an LED screen the maker calls cool touch. It supports a fully recessed, semi recessed or flat wall mount into a standard wall cavity, so you can choose how much construction you want. The 60 inch width reads as a feature wall piece.

The tradeoff is that a cool touch screen is a marketing term. It means the glass is designed to stay cooler than a gas fire, not that the heater outlet is cool, and a 1500 watt element still produces hot air. Compared with the Silonn 50, it is wider but has no Wi-Fi app in the listing. Against the Antarctic Star 36, it is bigger and costs more.

It suits a wide sofa wall or a bedroom focal wall. Match the mounting mode to your wall depth and check the manual for clearance. In year three, expect to clean the vents, replace remote batteries and keep fabrics and cables away from the heat outlet.
products.bestFor: A wide feature wall that wants three install options and a broad thermostat.
pros: A 60 inch width suits a long sofa or a media wall
Thermostat range of 60 to 99 degrees gives fine control
Three install modes let you match wall depth
Heat can be switched off to run the flame alone
cons: No Wi-Fi app in the listing, so no remote pre-heating
The cool touch claim does not remove heat at the outlet

products.name: Antarctic Star 36 Inch Electric Fireplace, Recessed or Wall Mounted

specList.label: Install
specList.value: Recessed, semi recessed or wall mounted

products.description:
Antarctic Star sells a 36 inch linear fireplace that can be recessed, semi recessed or wall mounted, with a front heater blower on 750 or 1500 watt settings and a thermostat. The flame comes from high intensity LEDs that the maker says burn high enough to look real. It is the lowest cost tier in this comparison, and a versatile entry point.

The tradeoff is that a 36 inch unit is a modest size and the plain styling is more practical than showy. Compared with the Garvee 30, it is wider but shares a similar heater. Against the Silonn 50, it has no app and is 14 inches narrower. A front blower means you must not block the front with furniture.

It suits a small living room, a nook or a bedroom. Check the stud positions and the recess depth, and keep curtains and cables clear of the front. In year three, expect to vacuum the vents, check the remote and clean the glass front with a soft cloth.
products.bestFor: Small to medium rooms where a low cost 36 inch unit is enough.
pros: Lowest cost tier of the six fireplaces
Recessed, semi recessed or surface mount options
Thermostat and two heat settings control comfort
A 36 inch width fits above a console or a small wall
cons: Plain styling and a narrow width give less presence
Front blower needs clear space in front

products.name: Garvee 30 Inch Ultra Thin Electric Fireplace, Wall Mounted or Recessed

specList.label: Install
specList.value: Recess into a 2 by 6 stud wall or surface mount

products.description:
Garvee's 30 inch ultra thin fireplace has 12 flame colours, 750 and 1500 watt heat settings and a thermostat from 62 to 82 degrees Fahrenheit, with touch and remote controls. The listing gives a specific recess spec: it fits a 2 by 6 stud wall for a flush look, or mounts on the surface. That detail is useful for planning, since a 2 by 6 bay is about 5.5 inches deep.

The tradeoff is size: 30 inches is small, and the thermostat window of 62 to 82 degrees is narrower than the Tehanld. It is best for an office, bedroom or a narrow living room wall. Compared with the Antarctic Star, it is smaller. Against the Silonn 50, it is far simpler.

It suits a small wall, a reading nook or a bedroom. If recessing, find studs and check the cavity before cutting drywall. In year three, vacuum the vents, check the touch panel and keep the front clear.
products.bestFor: Small walls and nooks that want flame and 1500 W of heat in a compact unit.
pros: Compact 30 inch width suits a nook, a bedroom or an office
Fits a 2 by 6 stud wall for a flush recessed finish
Two heat settings and a thermostat control warmth
Touch panel plus remote control
cons: Small footprint gives it little presence on a large wall
Narrower thermostat range than the 60 inch Tehanld

buyingCriteria.explanation: A fireplace should read as a feature, not a vent. Pick a width of roughly half to two thirds of the wall or furniture below, so 50 inches suits a sofa of 84 inches. The common mistake is choosing a unit from a narrow stud bay measurement instead of the visual width.

Wall mounted units hang from a bracket, while recessed units sit in a framed cavity. A 2 by 6 stud wall is about 5.5 inches deep, and the LegendFlame Austin is 5.8 inches deep. Measure the wall and check studs, wiring and drywall before you choose.

A 1500 watt plug in heater produces about 5100 BTU, which is supplemental heat for a single room. Whole room or whole house heating needs a real system. The Silonn lists 5100 BTU, and the Garvee and Antarctic Star list 750 and 1500 watt settings.

A thermostat cycles the heater, which reduces noise and power use. Ranges differ, from 62 to 82 degrees on the Garvee to 60 to 99 degrees on the Tehanld. App control, as on the Silonn, adds pre-heating.
LED flames range from flat colour to layered ember beds. Colour modes, ember media and brightness vary, and none replaces a real fire. Choose by how it looks in a dark room, not in the listing photo.
Electric fireplaces still make heat, so follow the manual for clearance from furniture, curtains and a TV above. Never block the vents, and keep pets and children away from the front.

specDecoder.watchFor: The Silonn 50 lists 5100 BTU, a standard figure for a plug in unit.

specDecoder.meaning: Two heat settings. 1500 watts draws about 12.5 amps at 120 volts, so use a dedicated circuit when possible.
specDecoder.watchFor: The Garvee, Antarctic Star and Tehanld list both settings.

specDecoder.watchFor: The Tehanld and Antarctic Star list all three.

howWeEvaluated.title: Width and install
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared widths from 30 to 72 inches and install types, noting stated depths such as 5.8 inches. We did not measure any unit.

howWeEvaluated.title: Heater and controls
howWeEvaluated.description: We read wattage, BTU and thermostat ranges and noted whether an app is offered. We treated heat as supplemental, not whole room.

howWeEvaluated.title: Flame display
howWeEvaluated.description: We looked at colour counts and ember effects, such as 12, 20 and 30 modes. These are described by makers, not verified by us.

howWeEvaluated.title: Safety information
howWeEvaluated.description: We noted cool touch claims, clearance needs and vent placement. We stated what listings do not say.

howWeEvaluated.title: Owner feedback patterns
howWeEvaluated.description: We researched common complaints about electric fireplaces, such as fan noise and remote failures. These shaped the cons. We did not use ratings or review counts.

cards.label: Wall mounted
cards.text: The Silonn, Tehanld, Antarctic Star and Garvee can hang on the surface, which needs a bracket and a stud. It is the easiest DIY route.

cards.label: Recessed
cards.text: The LegendFlame and Touchstone sit in the wall for a flush look, but need framing, power and trim work.

howToChoose.note: Choose wall mounted for speed and recessed for a built in look.

cards.label: Look for
cards.text: A width of half to two thirds of the wall, a thermostat, clear stated depth and a plan for studs, power and clearance.

cards.label: In this comparison
cards.text: The Silonn 50 suits most living rooms, and the Tehanld or LegendFlame suits a wide feature wall.

cards.label: Spend more if
cards.text: You want a built in look, a 60 or 72 inch width, or app control and good heat for a main living room.

cards.label: Save if
cards.text: The room is small, heat is secondary, or the unit is for a bedroom or office.

maintenance.why: Dust blocks airflow and makes the heater work harder. A soft brush on a vacuum clears the grille.
Fingerprints and dust show on the front. A dry microfibre cloth avoids scratches.
A warm or loose plug is a warning. Re-seat it and replace it if it discolours.
A dead remote is the most common reason a unit seems dead. Keep spares near the unit.
Letting the flame run occasionally keeps the electronics active. Switch the heater off in warm months.

faq.q: Can an electric fireplace heat a living room?
faq.a: It can warm a single room of about 300 to 400 square feet as supplemental heat, but not a whole home. A 1500 watt unit produces about 5100 BTU.
Plug in units need only an outlet, but recessing needs framing and often a nearby outlet. Hardwired units need an electrician.

faq.q: Can I mount a TV above one?
faq.a: Only if the manual allows it. Front venting units need clearance above, and heat can affect a TV, so check the manual first.

faq.q: Do they use a lot of power?
faq.a: A 1500 watt heater draws the same as other space heaters at the high setting. The flame alone uses very little.

faq.q: Are they safe to leave on?
faq.a: They are safer than open flames, but they make heat. Keep fabrics and pets away and never leave one unattended with blocked vents.

faq.q: What is the difference between recessed and wall mounted?
faq.a: Recessed sits in the wall for a flush look and needs framing. Wall mounted hangs on a bracket and is simpler.
